tasks.title: Establish the repository foundation
tasks.objective: Create the smallest Rust and TypeScript workspace, shared quality commands, CI, and package boundaries needed for the first executable vertical slice.
tasks.outcome: A clean checkout has one documented command that formats, analyzes, builds, and tests every initialized workspace without carrying unused framework code.
acceptance: Rust and TypeScript workspace boundaries follow docs/architecture.md and contain no placeholder plugin system.
A clean checkout can run the documented format, static analysis, build, and test commands.
CI executes the same repository-owned checks used locally.

verification.proves: The repository-owned quality boundary succeeds from a clean checkout.

tasks.title: Deliver a durable native Run
tasks.objective: Implement one daemon-owned local Run through a versioned public boundary with start, attach, detach, reconnect, input, output, resize, exit, and stop behavior.
tasks.outcome: A real child process survives client exit and can be reattached and controlled without relying on private implementation access.
acceptance: The daemon is the sole owner of the PTY, child process, Run identity, ordered output, and lifecycle state.
A real child process survives attach-client termination and remains usable after reconnect.
Invalid lifecycle transitions and unsupported behavior return explicit errors.

verification.proves: The native Run lifecycle integration tests pass through the public boundary.

tasks.title: Prove CLI and TypeScript client parity
tasks.objective: Expose the durable Run lifecycle through a real CLI client and the first TypeScript SDK without letting either client own runtime state.
tasks.outcome: CLI and TypeScript consumers can manage the same Run through the same versioned daemon boundary and observe consistent state and events.
acceptance: The CLI and TypeScript SDK exercise the same public protocol rather than separate runtime paths.
Closing either client leaves a durable Run alive unless stop was explicitly requested.
The SDK has no Electron, React, or editor dependency.

verification.proves: Cross-client lifecycle and state parity tests pass.

tasks.title: Map architecture and critical technical choices
tasks.objective: Turn the implemented system and target boundaries into one current-versus-target architecture map, core scenario model, and linked decision inventory.
tasks.outcome: A new contributor can follow every important lifecycle path and open one dedicated document for each critical implemented, provisional, or open technical choice.
acceptance: docs/architecture.md distinguishes current guarantees from target design and maps system context, components, Run ownership, core scenarios, ordering, failure semantics, and maturity gaps.
Every critical technical choice has one linked document with status, context, decision, alternatives, constraints, local repository evidence, wrong-case section, fixture mapping, and open questions.
Architecture and decision documents do not claim unimplemented Integration, fork, persistence, or tmux behavior as current capability.

verification.proves: The architecture entrypoint exposes current and target boundaries, key flows, and the decision index.

tasks.title: Research the technical-choice wrong-case corpus
tasks.objective: Conduct bounded multi-track web research for every critical choice and preserve real failures, incidents, anti-patterns, edge cases, and counterevidence as durable source-backed records.
tasks.outcome: Each decision document has an evidence-backed wrong-case section and every retained case is indexed with its failure mechanism and ctxmux invariant.
acceptance: The researcher workspace contains a charter, survey or bounded pass, per-choice tracks, primary-source cards, source-bound summaries, claims, counterevidence, and quality and drift evidence.
Every critical choice document cites retained cases and separates observed source claims from ctxmux-facing inferences and transfer limits.
docs/architecture/casebook.md maps each case to its choice, source, failure mechanism, protected invariant, and fixture disposition.

verification.proves: The source-backed wrong-case corpus is normalized and traceable to technical decisions.

tasks.title: Materialize wrong cases as continuous fixtures
tasks.objective: Convert the retained casebook into a validated fixture corpus and executable regressions for capabilities that ctxmux currently implements.
tasks.outcome: Known failures become a maintained ratchet: current-scope cases run continuously, and future-scope cases carry explicit activation conditions instead of silent gaps.
acceptance: Every retained case has a machine-readable fixture record linking choice, source, failure mechanism, preconditions, action, oracle, platform, tags, and fixture files or explicit activation blocker.
Applicable P0 lifecycle, protocol, replay, PTY, TypeScript, codegen, and CLI cases have executable tests that validate ctxmux invariants rather than dependency-specific incidental output.
scripts/check.sh and CI validate fixture schema and run all active fixtures; decision documents and casebook link to the resulting test evidence.
Cases for unimplemented Integration, fork, persistence, or tmux behavior remain explicitly inactive until the owning feature task implements that capability.

verification.proves: The repository gate validates the case corpus and executes every active wrong-case fixture.

tasks.title: Close native launch rollback ownership
tasks.objective: Make native Run launch transactional after child spawn so every later setup failure terminates and reaps the child before the failed start returns.
tasks.outcome: A rejected native launch publishes no Run and leaves no live child or zombie, without introducing a speculative Backend framework.
acceptance: Every failure after spawn_command and before Run publication terminates and reaps the owned child.
Deterministic owner-controlled fixtures cover reader, writer, output-thread, and waiter-thread setup failures without test-only unsafe or native code.
The correction stays inside the native launch owner and does not add a public Backend abstraction, plugin system, or general fault-injection framework.

verification.proves: The launch rollback fixture and the full native Run lifecycle gate pass.

tasks.title: Add explicit Integrations and the first coding Agent
tasks.objective: Introduce host-registered TypeScript Integrations only after the generic lifecycle works, then prove the contract with a shell and one mainstream coding Agent.
tasks.outcome: A client can explicitly register an Integration for detection, launch planning, capabilities, and semantic events while the daemon remains Agent-neutral.
acceptance: Integrations are ordinary explicitly imported TypeScript packages with no discovery service or plugin marketplace.
Agent-specific data does not enter the daemon's foundational Run types.
The raw Run remains operable when no semantic Integration observer is attached.

verification.proves: Generic Run and first-Agent Integration tests pass without separate client behavior.

tasks.title: Implement explicit context fidelity and fork
tasks.objective: Deliver portable Level A fork and prove Integration-provided Level B context fidelity with artifacts and lineage.
tasks.outcome: Clients can request and inspect a precise fork level, trace lineage, and receive an explicit unsupported result rather than a silent fidelity downgrade.
acceptance: Level A copies only the documented portable Run specification and declared input references.
Forks record parentage and declared workspace, artifact, and context references.
One Integration demonstrates a genuine Level B resume or fork.
A Level B request against a Level A-only Integration fails closed.

verification.proves: Fork fidelity, lineage, and fail-closed capability tests pass.

tasks.title: Close foundation at M3 and bind successor Features
tasks.objective: Close the completed runtime foundation without carrying persistence, tmux, composition, or release work inside one permanent umbrella Feature.
tasks.outcome: The foundation has an accurate terminal Goal and each post-foundation capability has one reviewed successor Feature with explicit dependency and acceptance truth.
acceptance: The foundation Goal and task plan stop at the completed M0 through M3 boundary.
Persistence/recovery, tmux, and composition/release each have one reviewed Feature and bounded Goal.
The release Feature depends on the persistence and tmux capability Features rather than absorbing their implementation.
T-006 and T-007 retain explicit supersession lineage and the full Tracker validates.

verification.proves: The durable roadmap defines the foundation closure and three successor delivery boundaries.
The repository remains green at the foundation closeout boundary.
